summary: CosmoDetective developed Earth System Trend Detective, an interactive web app that helps people explore 45 years of NASA Earth-observation data across cities and climate regions of the Indian subcontinent. Users can select a location, variable, season, and time period to examine trends in rainfall, temperature, aerosols, humidity, and related indicators. The app explains whether a trend is statistically significant, shows the yearly evidence behind it, tests forecast performance, and presents uncertainty clearly. It also supports comparisons between variables, event-based exploration, and user-uploaded time-series data. By translating complex climate data into understandable evidence, the project helps students and communities ask better questions about environmental change and local impacts.
details:
Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive web app that turns long-term Earth-observation time series into clear, testable environmental insights. Users choose a location, climate variable, season, and time range; the app then visualizes yearly patterns, calculates trends, indicates whether changes are statistically meaningful, and communicates uncertainty. It also enables comparisons between variables, exploration of extreme events, forecast checks, and upload of a user’s own time-series data.

The project makes climate and environmental evidence easier to understand for students, communities, and decision-makers. Instead of presenting a chart without context, it encourages users to ask: Is this change real? How strong is the evidence? What might it mean locally? Our intended impact is to build data literacy and support better-informed conversations about changing rainfall, temperature, aerosols, humidity, and related Earth-system conditions.

We developed the project as a responsive web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, then published it online with Netlify. We used web-based design, presentation, and AI voice/video tools to communicate the concept clearly. Its creativity comes from combining scientific trend analysis with a detective-style experience: users investigate evidence rather than simply consume results. We considered accessibility, simple language, mobile-friendly design, transparent uncertainty, and making complex environmental data approachable for non-specialists.
